items.actClause:
AN ACT to establish a commission to be known as the "New York seawall study
commission"; and providing for the repeal of such provisions upon expiration
thereof
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S3435

SPONSOR: ADDABBO
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to establish a commission to be known as the
"New York seawall study commission"; and providing for the repeal of
such provisions upon expiration thereof

 
PURPOSE:

To set up a commission to study the feasibility, costs, impacts, and
locations of a seawall around the city of New York's coastline.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Sets up a 13 member commission(appointed for the life of the commis-
sion)as follows

-3 members appointed by the  temporary president of the Senate
-1 member appointed by the minority leader of the Senate
-3 members appointed by the speaker of the Assembly
-1 member appointed by the minority leader of the Assembly
-5 members appointed by the Governor

The commission will hold hearings across the state and conduct a compre-
hensive study on sea levels and a potential seawall on the New York City
coastline. The matters studied by the commission shall include, but not
be limited to:

-Coastal areas at greatest risk from sea level rise;the future -Areas at
risk from storm surge with current sea levels;being created surge along
the
-Areas that are likely to be at risk from coastal hazards in through
year 2100; and
-The feasibility, costs, impacts, and locations of a seawall to protect
the city of New York from sea level rise and storm entire coastline

Amended Provisions:

Changes the commission from a 13 to a 14 member commission

-Commissioner of environmental conservation or his/her designee
-Secretary of State or his/her designee
-2 members appointed by the Governor
-2 members appointed by the temporary president of the senate -2 members
appointed by the Speaker of the Assembly -1 member appointed by the
leader of the Senate
-1 member appointed by the minority leaderofthe Assembly
-2 members to be appointed by the Mayor ofNYC
-1 member appointed by the County ExecutiveofNassau
-1 member appointed by the County ExecutiveofSuffolk

Allows recommendations on state and local regulatory and/or statutory,
alterations.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

In just the last few years, we have seen one horrific storm after anoth-
er. These once in a lifetime storms are becoming more and more common.
New York City must be prepared for the next Hurricane Sandy.  A seawall
is one idea that could possibly save lives in the next super-storm, as
well as protect vital infrastructure that could cost billions to repair.
This piece of legislation would create a commission to study the New
York City coastline to determine the feasibility of a seawall. In 1900,
a Category 4 hurricane, the "Great Storm", struck Galveston, Texas kill-
ing 6,000 to 12,000 individuals.  It was the deadliest natural disaster
in U.S history. In 1915, a similar storm in strength struck Galveston,
but the seawall proved invaluable for protection of the city and its
residents. A seawall as seen in Galveston, can help save lives and
protect infrastructure. A study of how such a seawall can be of vital
service to the New York City coast makes perfect sense.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2018: S6927A - PASSED THE SENATE; vetoed by Governor. Veto Memo 338

 
FISCAL IMPACT:

None

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

summary: Establishes a commission to be known as the "New York seawall study commission" which will study the feasibility, costs, impacts, and best locations for construction of a seawall or sea gate being created to protect the city of New York from sea level rise and storm surge along the entire coastline.
